# Purpose

This R Markdown document demonstrates an analysis workflow using **synthetic** marks. It explains the input data, processing steps, and expected output. The learner must review the R code and personally run and verify every calculation.

## Inputs

The synthetic dataset has six fictional student IDs and assessment marks on a 0–100 scale. The values are illustrative and are not personal information.

```{r input-data}
marks <- data.frame(
  student_id = paste0("S", 1:6),
  score = c(72, 85, 91, 68, 77, 89)
)
marks
```

## Processing Steps

The following sections validate the synthetic input, calculate descriptive statistics, and create a chart. The calculations must be run and checked independently by the student.

## Data Validation

Check the structure and mark range before analyzing.

```{r validation}
stopifnot(is.numeric(marks$score))
stopifnot(all(!is.na(marks$score)))
stopifnot(all(marks$score >= 0 & marks$score <= 100))
str(marks)
```

## Summary Statistics

The following code provides a starting point for calculating the mean, median, minimum, and maximum. Run it yourself, then independently verify each result.

```{r summary}
summary_stats <- data.frame(
  statistic = c("Mean", "Median", "Minimum", "Maximum"),
  value = c(mean(marks$score), median(marks$score),
            min(marks$score), max(marks$score))
)
summary_stats
```

## Visualization

A base R bar chart displays the fictional students' marks.

```{r plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
barplot(
  marks$score,
  names.arg = marks$student_id,
  main = "Synthetic Student Marks",
  xlab = "Fictional Student ID",
  ylab = "Score",
  ylim = c(0, 100),
  col = "steelblue"
)
```

## Outputs

- Printed synthetic input table.
- Printed summary statistics table.
- Bar chart of marks by fictional student ID.

## Limitations

The dataset is synthetic and very small. The analysis is illustrative, not suitable for generalizing about real student performance.
